claim_types.contains: the target genuinely contains or derives from the query. FoodOn simply fails to connect them.
claim_types.may_contain: commonly but not necessarily derived from the query; feedstock is a producer choice.
claim_types.cross_reactive: immunologically related; the allergen protein is NOT present.
claim_types.disputed: appears on avoidance lists without an established containment basis.
claim_types.shared_compound: the query and the target share the compound that drives a non-immune intolerance response. Neither derives from the other, and no allergen protein is involved; the compound is the same molecule whatever its origin.

overrides.reason: FoodOn asserts `peanut plant is_a nut producing plant`, defensible botanically but wrong for allergens: FALCPA treats peanut and tree nut as SEPARATE allergens. Without this a tree-nut query returns peanut and its 91-node closure. The two FoodOn sub-branches that exclude peanut cover only 4 of 7 major tree nuts between them, so there is no clean class to resolve to instead. Confirmed by Matt 2026-09-09: disconnect in both directions.
overrides.source: FDA FALCPA allergen list treats peanut and tree nuts separately
overrides.reverse_direction_note: The peanut -> tree nut direction needs no override and deliberately has none. peanut's closure already contains no tree nut, because the only link is an UPWARD is_a edge the invariant never traverses. A symmetric override would also be unsafe: peanut sits INSIDE nut food product's closure, so suppressing that closure from a peanut query would delete the peanut results themselves. Enforced structurally and guarded by tests in test/resolution_run.py.

overrides.reason: `bovine meat food product is_a cow food product`, and `cow food product` carries `in taxon Bos taurus`. The species pivot then walks back down from the taxon and reaches everything else bovine, including `cow milk`, `cheddar cheese` and 675 more dairy classes -- so a BEEF query told a diner to avoid milk. Beef and milk are separate avoidances: FALCPA lists milk as an allergen and beef not at all, and someone who avoids beef for religious or dietary reasons is usually not avoiding dairy. Suppressing `milk` for this root takes the closure from 1,555 to 785 and dairy from 677 to 25, while keeping beef steak, ground beef patty, beef jerky, beef broth and beef liver.
overrides.source: the same pattern as the peanut/tree-nut remove: ontologically real, wrong for avoidance
overrides.reverse_direction_note: The milk -> beef direction needs no override and has none: a milk query resolves to `milk`, whose closure contains no beef, because reaching beef would require ascending to Bos taurus and the invariant never ascends.

overrides.source: citrus intolerance is commonly a response to the acid rather than to the fruit proteins; the additive (E330) delivers it without any citrus in the product
overrides.review_note: signed: intolerance support, not allergy. Matt 2026-09-11 -- "I'd be looking for support of an intolerance response. It doesn't need to classify as an allergy." Attached to every citrus query root that resolves -- the genus, the fruit class and each species -- because someone with this intolerance says "lemon" or "orange" far more often than "citrus", and a weak claim is matched on the resolved root, not inherited down the hierarchy.

The label-convention repair pass could not see it because the convention it follows is `<X> food product -> <X> plant` and the source here is named `rye`, not `rye bread`.
overrides.source: FoodOn asserts no source on the class; the variants beneath it are all reached through the rye plant

overrides.reason: Mayonnaise is an emulsion of oil in egg yolk; the yolk is the emulsifier and is what makes it egg. FoodOn asserts no source on the class at all, so an egg query reached neither mayonnaise nor its six preparation variants -- 160 ingredient uses across the 5,000-recipe corpus, and the single largest false negative the family sweep could find. `egg yolk` rather than `chicken egg` because the yolk is the part actually used; both give the same +7, and the yolk is inside the egg closure so the transitive path holds either way.
overrides.source: FoodOn asserts no derives-from on mayonnaise, mayonnaise food product, or any of the six variants; only `mayonnaise with smoked salmon` has one, pointing back at mayonnaise itself

overrides.reason: The family class, bridged for the same reason as `mayonnaise` itself. Avoidance descends and never ascends, so bridging the child does not reach the parent: an ingredient that resolved to `mayonnaise food product` rather than `mayonnaise` would still have been missed by an egg query. The two classes have identical closures, so this adds only the family class itself.
overrides.source: same gap as the class beneath it: FoodOn asserts no source on either

entry_types.add: inject a claim the ontology does not make. Only claim `contains` enters the closure.
entry_types.remove: suppress a subtree that is ontologically real but not avoidance-relevant for one query.
entry_types.declined: reviewed and rejected. Kept so the reasoning is not lost.
entry_types.superseded: was correct and signed, and is now carried by structure instead. Inert, kept for the audit trail; test/override_run.py asserts the structural route still holds.
